name: PT Bakrie & Brothers Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bakrie & Brothers: a book-value discount, a pledged CCT loan and a konglo premium
frontmatter.summary: BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed vehicle: a toll road to 2061, an EV sibling, and steel and digital businesses. The toll road is marked at the midpoint of the house DCF and the acquisition-accounting fair value of the assets bought in 2025, above cost by the bargain gain; the EV stake at its house value. Nine-month revenue rose but interest outran operations. The fundamental is below the price; the konglo lens carries the target. HOLD, on the bull tail.
thesis: The toll road is marked at the midpoint of two sourced marks, not at book: the house DCF's equity value sits well below the 4,101 accounting fair value of the net assets acquired - that fair value itself exceeds the 3,781 consideration actually paid, by the 320 bargain gain - and the base carries the average of the two. The fair value is the bull mark, the DCF at the house cost of capital the bear.

The EV sibling is marked at the covered house fundamental, not at its listed premium and not at book. The market marks are disclosed in the valuation section and deliberately not used, as the konglo card requires.

The DCF is published with its rate, growth and present value, so the reader can test it: it sits below the acquisition fair value even at a project cost of capital, and falls below the debt at the house rate.

Governance is the discount's DNA and the record is fuller than the last draft said: a documented share pledge secures the Bank Nobu CCT-acquisition loan, most of the cash sits at the same bank, and a large stock of short-term investments and advances sits in offshore structures.

HOLD is a lens call, not a fundamental one: the fundamental value is well below the price, the base regime path is still below the price, and the target is reached only through the regime bull. The expected return is slightly negative and the cushion is the tail, not the parts.

catalysts.event: Maturity of the twelve-month Bank Nobu term loan that finances the CCT acquisition and is secured by the BNBR share pledge
The 2026 toll tariff adjustment on the Cimanggis-Cibitung section
Full-year 2026 results, the first audited read on post-rights interest cover and on the Nobu facility
Annual shareholders' meeting and any decision on the accumulated-loss position and a dividend
Regime - MSCI's decision on moving Indonesia to Standalone status

blocks.text: **What changed.** The third-quarter result is in, and it extends the nine-month picture rather than changing it. Nine-month revenue of **4,126** compares with **2,654** a year earlier, gross profit of **1,132** with **497**, operating profit of **596** with **26**, and the parent's line at **-342** against **12**, because interest and financial charges of **815** outran operating profit [S29]. Our FY2026E already reproduced that run-rate, so the revenue path, both margins, the cost of debt and the two book marks carry forward unchanged: this run rolls the model onto the filed quarter and changes no assumption.

The primary mark is now a genuine sum of three parts. The toll road is carried at the midpoint of the published house DCF and the acquisition-accounting fair value of the net assets acquired in November 2025; the EV sibling at the covered house fundamental; the rest of the group at its book value at 31 December 2025, which no longer moves when the other two marks move. The fundamental value is **Rp21** and the target **Rp38**. The rating stays **HOLD** because the konglo lens, not the fundamental, carries the target: the price is **Rp40**, the expected total return **-3.9%**, and the fundamental value is below the price with no margin of safety.

**The call.** HOLD at **Rp38**, with a twelve-month fundamental value of **Rp21** below today's price; the base regime path is **Rp37**, also below the price, and the target is reached only because the probability-weighted lens includes a bull at **Rp53**. That is a flow call on a thin float, not a view that the parts are worth the price.

Three things set the file. The value is one asset: the toll road, at net assets of **4,101** after the non-controlling-interest portion, with the project syndicated loan of **9,715** inside it [S12]. The nine months ran at a parent loss of **-342** because interest and financial charges of **815** exceeded operating profit of **596** [S29]. The balance sheet is opaque: short-term investments are **1,218**, advances for investment **901**, and **750** of the **954** cash balance sits at Bank Nobu, the lender that holds the pledge [S29].

What moves the value is the tariff schedule and traffic, the floating rate, and whether the manufacturing, EV and digital businesses ever earn their cost of capital [S12, S29]. The mark on the toll road is the single largest judgement in the file: the DCF and the acquisition-accounting fair value bracket it, and the base takes the midpoint. The bull is that fair value plus the EV stake at the rights subscription price; the bear is the DCF at the house cost of capital and the discount at the top of its band.

BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed industrial and infrastructure vehicle. It reports three segments - infrastructure and manufacturing, fabrication and construction services, and trading, services and investment - and its largest business by FY2025 revenue was the steel, pipe and construction group PT Bakrie Metal Industries at **2,200**, alongside the electric-vehicle group VKTR at **1,080** and smaller infrastructure and digital arms [S2, S12].

The asset that matters is the toll road. PT Cimanggis Cibitung Tollways operates the section between the Cimanggis and Cibitung junctions as the final link of the outer ring network, with a concession to 10 August 2061; traffic in the eight months to August 2026 averaged **43,911** vehicles a day on **2,500** of revenue a day, above the company's own budget [S15, S18]. The group took its ownership from a minority to full control on 28 November 2025, buying out PT Sarana Multi Infrastruktur and PT Waskita Toll Road and taking over their shareholder loans [S12, S18]. The subsidiary note shows **100.0%** legal ownership through Bakrie Toll Indonesia, while the acquisition accounting carries a non-controlling-interest portion that implies a lower effective share; the filing does not reconcile the two, and we use the filed mark rather than gross up [S12, F44].

The rest of the group is smaller and thinner than its revenue suggests: steel and pipe into oil, gas and infrastructure; automotive components; EV buses; and early-stage solar and construction-printing ventures [S2, S15]. None carries a separately disclosed segment profit, which is why the residual is a book figure rather than a bottom-up mark.

Control is family-based and indirect. The stated controlling shareholders are Aburizal, Nirwan Dermawan and Indra Usmansjah Bakrie, through a chain of vehicles; the largest registered holder is an offshore company at **26.0%** and the public holding below five per cent each is **30.0%** at 31 December 2025 [S11].

The sectors are not one industry, and the house treats BNBR as a conglomerate. The macro regime tilts away from Indonesian rate-sensitive domestic demand, the wrong side for a group whose most valuable asset is a domestic toll concession and whose balance sheet is floating-rate [S0, S12].

The toll road is where the industry question lives. It is a regulated concession rather than a competitive business: the regulator sets the tariff and the term, and value comes from traffic growth over a period long enough that early debt service does not determine the outcome. Cimanggis-Cibitung is the final section of the outer ring, connecting the Soekarno-Hatta corridor to the Tanjung Priok hinterland [S22]. It is a genuinely good asset in a dense catchment, and its traffic is above both its internal budget and the company's comparison set [S15]. The concession is the scarce resource: the toll segment is closed to new entry, so economics are set by the tariff schedule and the traffic ramp. The risk is regulatory - the timing of a tariff adjustment is a policy decision - and financial, because the concession is levered.

The rest of the group is a challenger in industries where it has no pricing power: steel pipe and fabrication into oil, gas and infrastructure; automotive components into domestic purchasing power; electric vehicles dependent on public procurement and local-content rules [S2, S15]. Steel and fabrication are cyclical and import-exposed, the EV business is a policy creature, and neither has covered its cost of capital through the cycle [S12, S15].

Regulation and policy therefore dominate: toll tariffs are set by the regulator, the EV business depends on procurement and local-content rules, and infrastructure contracts are awarded by the state [S15]. The floating-rate project debt, which the company singled out when it explained the nine-month loss, makes the rupiah matter too [S26, S29].

On a five-forces reading the toll road has negligible new entry and no substitute in its corridor, so it is the only part worth close to its carrying value; manufacturing, components and EV face import competition and fragmented customers, and their returns reflect that [S12, S15]. The moat is the concession document, and it belongs to one subsidiary.

**The reported quarter.** Nine-month revenue, gross profit and operating profit all stepped up on the prior-year comparative, while the parent's line swung from a small profit to a loss as interest outran operations; the operating step is largely scope, because the toll road entered the group only on 28 November 2025 [S29]. The company attributes the revenue growth to Bakrie Metal Industries at **2,090**, VKTR at **1,060** and Bakrie Indo Infrastructure at **952** of nine-month revenue [S26].

**Actual versus our forecast.** Our FY2026E revenue of **5,662** is the nine-month actual plus the third quarter again, the gross margin of **27.4%** is the filed nine-month ratio, and the parent loss of **-376** is struck on the same post-rights interest base as the filing. The quarter confirms the base case and no input changes [S29, S0].

**The nine months.** Nine-month revenue also exceeds the whole of FY2025 (**3,743**), on company-reported EBITDA of **810** [S29, S26]. The parent nevertheless lost **-342**: operating profit plus a **5** disposal gain less a **2** FX loss, **815** of interest and **70** of other charges gives a pre-tax loss, and the **48** net tax charge together with the **9** profit allocated to non-controlling interests, deducted rather than added, take it to the parent loss [S29]. The tax is booked at profitable subsidiaries even though the group is in loss, so the engine would remove it; we carry it as a non-operating charge in FY2026E to reproduce the filed nine months.

**Debt and interest.** The rights issue cut gross debt to **2,054** of short-term and **11,275** of long-term loans at 30 September, against cash of **954** [S29]. The forecast runs the debt on that post-rights basis from FY2027E: FY2026E interest is struck on the opening balance because the issue closed in the third quarter, but the forward bill falls to about **903** [S29, S0]. Operating profit of **884** then covers interest about once in FY2027E and above once from FY2028E, rather than never - the red team's F5 correction. The forecast cash line is negative because the engine has no equity-issuance line; use the filed cash, not the modelled line. FY2026E interest is struck on the opening pre-rights balance, so it overstates the year by roughly a tenth against a post-rights blend; the forecast years run at the filed rate on the post-rights balance. Both are stated here rather than printed as forecast values.

**D&A and EBITDA convention.** The data pack is wrong on D&A: the audited FY2025 charge is **171** [S12], while the pack carries only the general-and-administrative allocation. The company's reported EBITDA of **810** is operating profit plus a depreciation add-back that excludes the **329** amortisation of the toll-road concession charged to cost of revenues [S29]. The model follows the company's convention; if the concession amortisation is added back too, EBITDA is higher and leverage lower.

Our forecast holds FY2026E revenue at the nine-month run-rate plus the third quarter again [S29, S26]. The gross margin is held at the nine-month **27.4%** and operating expenses at **13.0%** of revenue, the filed ratios, not the lower FY2025 ratios struck without the toll road [S29, S12]. FY2026E EBITDA is **1,112**, a **19.6%** margin; the step from FY2025 is scope, not margin expansion. The parent loss is **-376**, close to the nine-month actual [S0].

**Cash conversion, accruals and related parties.** The accruals ratio - net income less operating cash flow, over average total assets - is low in both audited years: FY2024 parent profit (328) against a small operating cash inflow, and FY2025 parent profit (494) against an operating cash OUTFLOW (-108), each over average assets of the two balance sheets. Both are far below the ten per cent flag, and the nine months to September 2026 is negative: net income of -342 against operating cash flow of 80. So no manipulation-class accruals flag. What the accruals ratio flatters is cash conversion: FY2025 EBITDA of 288 became an operating cash outflow once interest was paid, and the nine-month operating cash of 80 compares with reported EBITDA of 810. That is optics-class: disclosed, interest-driven, not fabricated. [S12, S29, F4, F65, F67, F88, F107, F108, F109]

The related-party channel is the item the method card makes us quantify. Quantified balances: the **3,662** payable to Hartman International at FY2025, which the July 2026 rights issue was raised to repay; **901** of advances for investment at 30 September 2026, of which **750** is Fortesque, an offshore structure, and **151** is Mandala Raya Yuwana; and **1,218** of third-party short-term investments. As a share of the balance sheet the advances are a low single-digit percentage of total assets of **25,541**, while the Hartman payable was a mid-teens share of FY2025 total assets; as a share of revenue the advances are about a fifth of the nine-month figure. The archived notes do not give a related-party revenue split, so the revenue channel is a disclosure gap rather than a clean bill. Classification: optics-class on the balance sheet (disclosed, secured, but offshore and unmarkable by a minority), manipulation-class on none. [S29, S12, F16, F77, F80, F81, F82, F87]

Capital allocation has run one way: towards the family's other vehicles and towards issuing shares. The 2024 quasi-reorganization removed **19,530** of accumulated deficit [S11, S12], and the July 2026 issue raised **4,714** and **263,337**m shares, most passed through to repay the BTI facility [S29, S19]. No dividend has been paid [S6]. The special-monitoring-board status is **unverified**: the archived exchange document is a list of issuers REMOVED from the board on 28 September 2026 and does not mention BNBR, and absence from a removal list does not establish absence from the board [S30]. We have not found a current membership list in the archive. That matters because a special-board listing would put the shares into full call auction and change every entry and exit assumption, so it is carried as an open item rather than a clean bill.

The house method for a conglomerate is a sum of parts, and the three lines now carry three separate marks. **Cimanggis-Cibitung: 4,101** is the acquisition-accounting fair value of the net assets acquired - not the price paid, which was 3,781 of consideration, the difference being the 320 bargain-purchase gain - and it is one of the two marks, not the mark. **VKTR: the covered sibling's house fundamental.** **The rest of the group:** **3,853** of parent book equity at 31 December 2025 less the book values of the two marked parts, which is negative and stays fixed when the other marks move. Because that residual is defined on 31 December 2025 book and does not move with the two marks, the total is no longer book equity by construction: the sum of parts differs from book by the net mark on the toll road plus the mark on the EV stake, which is what the method is supposed to measure.

Because the bull mark is that fair value rather than the price paid, the base midpoint carries the bargain gain: anchoring the bull at the 3,781 consideration would lower the bull mark by 320 and the midpoint by half of it, before the holdco discount. We keep the fair value because it is the audited acquisition-accounting value of the assets themselves, it is what the filing's balance sheet carries, and the consideration was struck with state shareholders in a distressed sale; the alternative anchor is disclosed here so the reader can halve the gain and see the lower midpoint [S12, F14, F44, F110].

**The toll-road DCF, published rather than asserted.** The assumptions file carries the full input set and the resulting present value and equity value - rate, growth path, present value and equity - but not a year-by-year schedule, because the engine's placeholder set has no key for a house project DCF; what is published is enough to reproduce the equity figure from the inputs. The inputs are sourced or stated: 2026 revenue from the daily run-rate, the FY2025 standalone EBITDA margin (694 on 846), concession amortisation from the filed charge, the statutory tax rate, maintenance capex, a decade of tariff indexation plus a traffic-ramp judgement and then inflation to the 10 August 2061 expiry, with no terminal value because the asset reverts to the state. The indexation is the house CPI/tariff path; the ramp above it is a house judgement that the toll-road source supports only qualitatively - "revenue is projected to continue increasing ... rising traffic projections" [S15] - and a CPI-only path is the stated sensitivity: it removes the ramp and pushes the DCF equity below the figure used here, deepening the bear mark. Discounted at the project's own cost of capital - the house pre-tax cost of debt on the facility and a typical toll-road equity return - the present value of the free cash flow covers the 9,715 syndicated loan with a thin equity cushion. Discounted at the house cost of capital of 12.0% the same cash flow does not cover the loan at all: that is the top of the rate range, and it is what the earlier "at or below zero" sentence described, not the base case. The DCF equity therefore sits below the acquisition fair value at every rate in the range rather than bracketing it, and the base takes the midpoint of the two. The fair value is the bull; the DCF at the house WACC, floored at zero, is the bear [S12, S22, S29, F15, F17, F18, F19, F33, F34, F35, F89, F94].

**The EV stake, with every mark disclosed.** VKTR is covered and its house twelve-month fundamental is used, not its listed price and not its book. The marks that are **not** used, so the reader can see the range: at today's market price the **3,661**m shares, diluted by **25.5%**, are worth several times the base mark; at the theoretical ex-rights price (**675**) and at the pre-ex price (**835**) they are worth an order of magnitude more; at the rights subscription price (**2,135**) they are still worth several times it. The base uses the sibling's house fundamental because the konglo card forbids a listed premium inside the parent's fundamental value, and because BNBR transferred its rights entitlement rather than funding it, so the subscription price is a floor a third party paid rather than the parent's cost. The bull mark step is that floor [S12, S23, S25, F37, F38, F39, F51, F57].

**The P/BV cross-check** is struck on premium-free peers at **0.73x** the filed post-rights book of **8,304**, which gives **Rp23** - materially ABOVE the primary. That divergence is the point, not a confirmation: the market capitalises filed book, while the primary marks the toll road below it, and the gap is the amount by which the two views of the same balance sheet differ. The P/E leg stays removed: FY2025 parent profit carries the **320** bargain-purchase gain and the **422** remeasurement gain, and the parent is loss-making from FY2026E through FY2034E before a small positive in the final forecast year [S12].

**The bridge** is the July 2026 rights proceeds of **4,714**, less the nine-month parent loss of **-342**, plus the **8,304**-reconciling other equity components, and it now ties to filed parent equity at 30 September 2026 [S29]. A holdco discount of **38%** is then applied, at the wide end of the band, for the flags the method card names [S11, S16]. The primary produces **Rp16** per share. The target and the price are printed rounded to the nearest rupiah, while the expected total return is struck on the unrounded target, so the printed pair does not reproduce the return exactly; the difference is rounding, not a second calculation.

**What the price implies.** The cost of capital is **12.0%** with a cost of equity of **17.8%** and a levered beta of **1.79**. At any discount in the method card's band the value is below the price, so the price pays a premium to the parts, not a discount [S0]. It pays for toll traffic and tariff growth above our DCF, for the EV order book, and for a manufacturing mark above book; none is sourced well enough to capitalise, and none is in the base.

**The konglo lens.** BNBR is a Bakrie-family holding vehicle with a free float of **23.4%** [S0]. The price is **2.25x** the blend fundamental of **17.8** that the lens uses today; measured against the twelve-month fundamental of **Rp21** the multiple is higher again, so the two ratios in this report are not the same denominator. The base regime scenario keeps **30%** of the log gap and gives **Rp37**, BELOW the price; the bear gives **Rp27** and the bull **Rp53**, and the probability-weighted target of **Rp38** is above the base path only because the bull carries a quarter of the weight. The premium is a regime variable, never an input [S0].

**Mark sensitivity, and an honest limitation.** The toll-road mark is the largest single number in the file: every billion of mark moves the fundamental by a few rupiah a share before the discount. The bear mark is the DCF at the house WACC and the bull mark is the acquisition-accounting fair value; the EV stake moves from the sibling's house fundamental in the base to the rights-floor mark in the bull. Those cases are NOT in the scenario values in the risk section, because the template's scenario engine can only shock model inputs and not holdings marks - a template limitation, stated rather than hidden. The scenario values therefore move the discount and the earnings path only, and the mark cases are described here and in the risk section instead of being dressed up as scenario arithmetic.

**Interest and refinancing (high likelihood, high impact).** Operating profit of **596** against interest and financial charges of **815** [S29]. The rights issue cut the debt and cover reaches about breakeven in FY2027E, but the loan is floating-rate and the Bank Nobu facility of **700** matures in November 2026 [S29].

**Pledged shares and the Nobu concentration (high likelihood, medium impact).** The Bank Nobu CCT-acquisition facility is secured by **2,000**m BNBR shares plus BTI, BRMS, ENRG and VKTR shares [S29]. The pledge is a margin-call and supply risk because the controller's vehicles set the float, and **750** of the **954** cash balance sits at the same lender, so the deposit may be compensating in substance [S29].

**Concentration and earnings quality (medium likelihood, high impact).** One asset, one concession, one corridor; the rights proceeds that make book positive sit in the bridge, not in the businesses [S12, S29]. FY2025 is dominated by a one-off gain, FY2024 by gains on loan settlements and asset sales, and the accumulated deficit was eliminated by a quasi-reorganization, so reported profit is not a guide [S11, S12].

**Equity issuance and liquidity (high likelihood, medium impact).** The July issue was struck at **53** a share, raised **4,714**, diluted a non-subscriber by up to **34%**, and the largest holders transferred their entitlement to a standby buyer rather than fund it [S29, S16, F27, F72]; VKTR's own issue diluted non-participating holders by **25.5%** [S25].

**Scenarios.** The probabilities are bear **25%**, base **50%** and bull **25%**. The lens already carries a regime bear, so the business scenarios no longer double-count it. The live methods are the book-value discount (fixed parts) and the P/BV leg (fixed book), so the spread is a discount-and- earnings sensitivity: the bear widens the discount to the top of the band, the bull narrows it, and neither shocks the CCT or VKTR marks. The bear gives **Rp20**, the base **Rp21** and the bull **Rp21** [S0].

**The konglo lens and the regime.** The business scenarios move the fundamental value; a second, independent set of regime scenarios moves the premium, keeping **30%** of the log gap in the base case for a target of **Rp38** (bear **Rp27**, bull **Rp53**) [S0]. The dated events are the minimum free-float step from March 2027, the HSC reviews, and MSCI's Standalone decision by 30 June 2027; another rights issue, a placement or a change of control are the other live catalysts [S0, S16].

Signposts that would change the view: a tariff adjustment materially above the scheduled one, interest cover turning positive on the post-rights balance, a funded plan showing the manufacturing and EV businesses earning their cost of capital, or any transaction that upstreams cash to the parent's shareholders.

The ultimate beneficial owners are the three Bakrie brothers; the largest registered holder is at **26.0%** [S11]. The register is not one large holder and a public tail: Fountain City Investment holds **22.2%**, UOB Kay Hian **8.5%**, Eurofa Capital **6.8%**, Levoca Enterprise **5.3%** and PT Biofuel Indo Sumatra **1.3%**, with the public below five per cent each at **30.0%** [S11]. Several large holders are offshore or nominee vehicles, so control is not proportionate to economic ownership.

**Pledged shares.** The last draft said pledges were not established. That was wrong. The short-term-loans note shows the Bank Nobu term loan for the CCT acquisition, still outstanding at **700** at 30 September 2026, secured by **2,000**m BNBR shares plus BTI, BRMS, ENRG and VKTR shares [S29]. The facility is twelve months from 19 November 2025 at **7.0%** and matures in November 2026; a margin call or a refinancing that requires more collateral is a near-term supply and control risk [S29, F100].

**Offshore and structured paper.** Total third-party short-term investments were **1,321** at 31 December 2025 and **1,218** at 30 September 2026 [S29]. The notes describe Bellridge exchangeable bonds and Sherwin and Fortesque placements. Advances for investment are **901**, comprising Fortesque **750** and Mandala Raya Yuwana **151**; the Fortesque funds sit in a designated account managed by Fortesque for BTI, and a Fortesque return was settled through the company's loan to MRY [S29]. They are assets, but they are offshore and structured, and a minority holder cannot mark them.

**Dividend-upstream coverage and look-through leverage.** No cash dividend has been paid and the payout is nil [S6]; the only distributions are to non-controlling interests [S29]. Look-through, the debt sits in the parts: the CCT syndicated loan of **9,715** is at the toll-road subsidiary and the BTI facility of **4,362** was at the intermediate holding level [S12, F15, F42]. The lenders hold the share pledge and set the covenants - the maximum debt-to-equity covenant is **6.2x** [S12] - so look-through leverage is worse than the headline.

| Look-through debt | IDR bn | Sits at | Source | |---|---|---|---| | CCT syndicated project loan, FY2025 | 9,715 | toll-road subsidiary | [S12, F15] | | BTI facility (Hartman and Bank Nobu), FY2025 | 4,362 | intermediate holdco | [S19, F42] | | Bank Nobu term loan, 9M26 | 700 | BTI / CCT acquisition | [S29, F84] | | Short-term loans, 9M26 | 2,054 | consolidated operating companies | [S29, F68] | | Long-term loans, 9M26 | 11,275 | consolidated, including CCT | [S29, F69] | | Cash, 9M26 | 954 | consolidated, of which Nobu 750 | [S29, F70, F79] |

The equity history is the governance issue with teeth: a sequence of capital increases and a 2024 quasi-reorganization that eliminated **19,530** of accumulated deficit [S11, S12]. The July 2026 issue continued the pattern: **4,714** of proceeds and **263,337**m shares, most passed through to repay the BTI facility rather than retained [S29, S16]. On ESG, nothing in the record suggests an exposure that changes the valuation [S11].

**The konglo profile.** BNBR is the Bakrie family's listed holding vehicle [S11, S16]. The registry free float is **23.4%**, above the exchange's minimum; the annual report's public-holding figure of **30.0%** is the share held below five per cent each at 31 December 2025, and the gap is definition and date [S0, S11]. BNBR is not on the HSC list as of 22 October 2026, so the HSC index exclusions do not apply; there is no enforcement action or index deletion recorded [S0].

The dated catalysts are in the frontmatter: the November 2026 maturity of the Bank Nobu facility that carries the share pledge, the 2026 tariff adjustment, the full-year results, and MSCI's Standalone decision. We watch the syndicated facility's rate at each amendment, traffic and revenue per day against budget, interest cover, the parent-attributable residual, whether VKTR becomes covered, whether the data-centre intention becomes a filed project, and any new pledge, rights issue or change in the share count - **263,337**m after the issue [S2, S12, S15, S29, S0].

bear.narrative: The discount widens to the top of the method card's 20-40% band as the family has to raise equity again to fund a group that still consumes cash; revenue growth is slower than the tariff adjustment implies; and the floating-rate cost of debt is higher after the post-rights structure settles. The red team's F8 is right that the earlier bear discount was outside the method card's band, so the shock is capped at the top of the band, and that the earlier business-bear probability double-counted the konglo lens's own regime bear, so it is cut to match the lens. The holdings marks are fixed by the engine, so the bear moves the discount and the earnings path, not the CCT or VKTR marks; the mark downside is the CCT DCF cross-check in §4, and the dilution risk is stated in the report rather than shocked.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows inside the band; the scheduled 2026 tariff adjustment and the Burangkeng interchange lift toll traffic faster than plan, so revenue growth is higher; and the cost of debt falls as the post-rights structure and the debt repayment settle. The bull's mark upside is shown separately in §4: VKTR re-marked to the Rp200 rights-issue floor against book and CCT left at its acquisition mark, because a house DCF does not support a higher CCT value. The engine's holdings are fixed, so that mark step is not a scenario shock; the scenario table is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is set from the filed nine-month result, not extrapolated from the first half: revenue of 4,125.792 in the nine months to September (F62) with the fourth quarter held at the third quarter's run-rate (nine months plus the third quarter again) implies a full year of about 5,662 and a step of about half on FY2025 [S29, F62]. The step is the full-year consolidation of the CCT toll road, which entered the group only on 28 November 2025, plus the disclosed increases at VKTR, Bakrie Metal Industries and Bakrie Indo Infrastructure [S26, S29]. Because that is a scope change and not a growth trend, the series steps down to a single-digit rate from FY2027E and holds at the house terminal rate thereafter: FY2027E is set at 8%, sourced to the scheduled 2026 CCT tariff adjustment and to traffic already running above the company's own budget (43,911 vehicles a day, F18), not to a forecast-year spike. [S26, S29, S12, S15, F18]

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026, the last actual: gross profit of 1,131.793 on revenue of 4,125.792 is 27.4% of revenue (F63, F62), up from the 25.1% first-half ratio and from FY2025's 19.9%, because FY2025 held only one month of a toll road whose gross margin is far above the manufacturing average; the toll road alone ran at 846 revenue and 694 EBITDA in FY2025 on a standalone basis (F33, F34), so weighting the parts lifts the blended margin [S29, S12, S22]. The third quarter carried a higher margin than the first half; we do not extrapolate that quarter on its own, and the nine-month ratio is the neutral anchor. Held flat after FY2026E: no disclosed contract or tariff schedule justifies a further step. [S29, S12, S22]

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026: total operating expenses of 535.548 on revenue of 4,125.792 are 13.0% of revenue (S29), below the 14.2% first-half ratio and FY2025's 16.8%, which were struck on smaller revenue bases. The nine-month figure is the last actual and already carries the operating-expense mix of a group with the toll road consolidated for the whole period; the third quarter was lighter still, and we do not extrapolate that quarter on its own. The 16.8% audited ratio was Total Beban Usaha of 627.521 on revenue of 3,742.973 (F54, F52, S12). No cost programme is disclosed that would take it lower. [S29, S12]

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026: the company's reported EBITDA of 810.25 less operating profit of 596.245 implies depreciation and amortisation of about 214 on revenue of 4,125.792, i.e. 5.2% of revenue (S26, S29); the fixed-asset depreciation note alone shows 105.313 for the nine months (S29), and the balance is concession and intangible amortisation, which the pack's D&A line omits. The audited FY2025 charge was 171.363 (F6) against the data pack's 22.921, which is the general-and-administrative allocation only. [S29, S26, S12, F6]

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Set from the filed nine-month cash-flow statement: acquisitions of fixed assets of 270.782 on revenue of 4,125.792 are 6.6% of revenue, with the toll rest area, the EV assembly facility and the steel businesses still consuming capital and a further 59.744 spent on toll concession rights (S29); no archived source discloses a taper. [S29]

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 ratio (operating working capital of 1,453.9 on revenue of 3,743.0), which is the last audited figure for a group whose receivables are heavily related-party. [S0]

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Set above the FY2025 reported rate of 3.1%, which is distorted by non-taxable bargain-purchase and restructuring gains, and at the low end of the Indonesian corporate range because the group carries tax losses forward after the quasi-reorganization. [S12, S11]

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the filed nine months to September 2026: gross interest on loans and financial charges of 849.451 (the net charge of 814.542 plus interest income of 34.909) against opening debt of 16,739.8 (F15 plus the year-end short- and long-term lines) annualise to about 6.8%, which is the rate this line carries [S29, F66]. That sits in the audited FY2025 band of 3%-10% (Rupiah) and 1%-7% (US dollar), with the toll road's 9,715.21 syndicated facility (F15) the largest single line [S12, F15]. The red team's F5 is right that the forecast must not run the whole horizon on the pre-rights balance: FY2026E interest is struck on the opening 16,739.8 because the rights issue closed at the end of July 2026 and the nine-month filed charge of 814.542 already carries seven months of pre-repayment interest, but the debt is restated to the filed 30 September 2026 balance of 13,328.9 from FY2027E through the negative net-borrowing line below, so the forward interest bill is about 902 rather than 1,202. The rate stays the filed 6.8%; the balance, not the rate, is what changes. [S29, S12, S19, F66, F68, F69]

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Set from the filed nine months: interest income of 34.909 annualised on the opening cash and short-term-investment balance the data pack carries (1,557.8) is about 3.0%, well below the disclosed time-deposit rates of 4.50%-6.75% (F48, S29 p.53) because most of the balance is working cash and short-term investments whose income is not all booked as interest. [S29, S12, F48]

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the actual fall in gross debt: the filed balance sheet shows 16,739.8 of interest-bearing debt at 31 December 2025 and 13,328.9 at 30 September 2026 (short-term 2,054.172 plus long-term 11,274.769), a reduction of 3,410.9 after the July 2026 rights issue repaid the BTI facility [S29, F68, F69]. Entering that reduction as negative net borrowing puts the FY2027E opening balance, and therefore the forward interest charge, on the filed post-rights basis, which is what the red team's F5 asks. The 4,713.8 of equity proceeds themselves stay in the valuation bridge: the engine's cash-flow template has no equity-issuance line, so the modelled cash balance turns negative once the repayment is entered - that is a template limitation, not a forecast, and the report quotes the filed 30 September cash of 954.353 and net debt of 12,374.6 instead of the modelled cash line. Later years are held at zero: with no dated new facility in the archive and no dividend, the base case assumes rolling maturities are refinanced flat rather than adding debt, which is a stated financing assumption, not a sourced plan. [S5, S12, S19, S29, F68, F69, F70, F72]

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the filed nine-month other charges of 69.515 plus the foreign-exchange loss of 2.246, net of the 5.166 gain on asset disposals, i.e. about 66.6 for the year (S29 notes 35 and 36), PLUS the filed nine-month net income-tax expense of 47.892 (current tax 62.064 less deferred 14.172) [S29, F90, F91, F92, F85, F86]. The tax must be carried here because the engine charges tax as pos(pbt) x rate and therefore books zero on a consolidated loss, while the company actually paid subsidiary-level current tax in the nine months despite the group loss - the red team's F6 is right. Carrying the 47.892 as a non-operating charge reproduces the filed parent loss instead of implying a profitable fourth quarter; the FY2026E parent loss then lands close to the nine-month actual rather than above it. The note describes the other items as non-operational receipts and payments individually below Rp10bn, so we take the actual once for this year rather than annualising it. Later years are held at zero: FY2025's other income of 401.969 was dominated by the 320.127 one-off gain on the CCT bargain purchase (F14) and no archived source forecasts a further one-off. [S29, S12, F14, F85, F86, F90, F91, F92]

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at 2% against the audited FY2025 ratio of 1.77%, reflecting the large non-controlling interest the consolidation carries (818.494 at 31 December 2025, of which 812.291 is VKTR, F45) and the fact that minorities absorb their share of the group's losses. [S12, F45]

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has paid no cash dividend in the period covered by the price history and its stated policy makes any payout conditional on financial condition, positive retained earnings and a shareholders' resolution; the last decision on record was to carry profit to retained earnings, and the group has just raised equity rather than returned it. [S6, S5]

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E carries the July 2026 rights issue at its filed terms: 14 new Series E shares for every 27 old, which is 0.5185185185 of the count in issue at the last filed balance sheet (F8, F9) [S16, S5]. The ratio is the exact filed one and reconciles the forecast share vector to the pro-forma total of 263,336.672m in F8; nothing is assumed after that.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for an Indonesian rupiah reporter: long-run nominal GDP, no company-specific claim. [S0]

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 38%, at the wide end of the 20-40% band the method card says a family holding company's discount persists in, not at the mid-band 33% the first draft used. The red team's C9 is right that 33% had no name-specific anchor; the anchor now used is the set of flags the card says keep a discount wide, every one of which this name carries: a controlling family whose stakes sit behind British Virgin Islands vehicles (F32), a public float of 29.98% (F31), serial equity issuance that has repeatedly reset the share count and most recently struck a rights issue at Rp53, a quasi-reorganization that eliminated 19,530 of accumulated deficit in 2024 (F30), and a dividend record of nil, so cash does not reach the parent's shareholders. The card's dividend-upstream law says a holdco that neither distributes nor covers its own costs deserves the widest discount in its range, which is what 38% is. The discount is applied and not narrowed: the method card makes the discount the base rate, not the opportunity, and this file has no dated discount-narrowing catalyst (no buyback, tender, asset sale, sub-IPO, simplification or control change is dated in the record), so the discount is not credited with narrowing. The 0.38 is a chosen discount level, not the archetype's probability of narrowing: the 'rate' field in data/base_rates.yaml is that success probability and is not read as the discount itself. BNBR's own five-year discount history cannot be computed here - no house sum-of-the-parts exists before this file - so the band plus the flags is the best available anchor. [S11, F30, F31, F32, S16]

challenges.challenge: The base carries CCT at 4,101 (F44) while section 4 and thesis line 3 say the house DCF puts the road's equity 'at or below zero'; the DCF is never quantified (no rate, growth, PV) and its result is in no scenario. On the report's own inputs (684 of annual operating cash flow, 34 years, 9,715 of debt) the PV at 10-12% and 0-3% growth is 5.6-8.7tn, so equity is -4.1tn to -1.0tn: the mark overstates nav by 4-6tn. Taking CCT to zero alone cuts nav from 8,225 to 4,124, the blend to about Rp12.4, the 12-month fundamental to about Rp14.6 and the lens target to about Rp24 (-40%): a SELL, not HOLD.
challenges.answer: The DCF is now published in full in the assumptions file (rate, growth path, PV 11,450, debt 9,715, equity 755 at a 10.5% project WACC, minus 783 at the 12% house WACC) and the toll road is re-marked in the base to the midpoint of that DCF and the 4,101 acquisition mark. The 'at or below zero' claim is gone, the acquisition mark is the bull and the DCF at the house WACC the bear. Fundamental falls from 20.1 to 17.8 and the target from 40 to 38.

challenges.challenge: The engine's primary 'sotp' is not a sum of parts: value = (F10 parent book equity + F72 - F67) x (1 - 38%), so the CCT/VKTR/residual rows net to the same book whatever marks are used, and the P/BV leg applies 0.73x to that same 8,304. The prose relabels the method but the model, weights and packet still call it sotp at 80%, and 'two methods' is one input with false precision.
challenges.answer: The arithmetic is now a genuine sum of parts: the residual is defined as the book value of the other businesses at 31 December 2025 and no longer moves when the two marks move, so the SOTP differs from book by the net mark. CCT is a house DCF mark and VKTR a covered sibling house fundamental, both independent of the residual, and the report states the pbv leg is materially above the primary rather than confirming it.

challenges.challenge: VKTR is the file's largest omitted upside: the 10.677bn shares (F37; 35:12 ratio per S23) are worth 7,207 at the Rp675 theoretical ex-rights price (F39) and 8,915 at Rp835 (F38). The base carries 262 at book and the report never discloses the market mark, while calling 2,135 (the Rp200 subscription price) the bull's 'principal upside' - a floor, not a bull - and even that step is excluded from the bull scenario value of 24.3.
challenges.answer: All VKTR marks are disclosed in the valuation section: the current market price, the theoretical ex-rights and pre-ex prices, the Rp200 subscription floor and the book value. The base now carries the covered sibling house fundamental per the konglo card rather than book, and the bull mark step is the rights floor; the template cannot shock holdings, stated openly.

challenges.challenge: The bear cannot lose money on the marks: the revenue-growth (-3pp) and cost-of-debt (+1.5pp) shocks have zero effect because value = fixed book x (1 - holdco discount); only the +2pp discount moves it, giving bear 23 vs base 24, a 4% spread. The downsides the report itself identifies (CCT DCF, VKTR dilution, the 901 advances and 1,218 short-term investments at book, a Nobu refinancing) are in no scenario.
challenges.answer: The base now carries the mark ambiguity itself (midpoint) and the report quantifies the bear mark (DCF at the house WACC, floored) and the bull mark (acquisition and rights floor) in a dedicated mark-sensitivity passage, with the scenario engine limitation stated rather than hidden. The old bear that moved only the discount is replaced by a base that already bears half the mark-down.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 and section 5 say the base regime scenario 'keeps 30% of the log gap and gives Rp40'; the model's base scenario is Rp38.3 (price 40, -4.2%) and Rp39.5 is the probability-weighted target, reached only because the 25% bull widens the premium to 2.21x. The summary repeats the framing, so the reader is told the modal path holds the price when it does not.
challenges.answer: The prose now uses the model's base regime path (about 37, below the price) and says explicitly that the 38 target is reached only because the bull carries a quarter of the weight. The summary and thesis no longer read as if the modal path holds the price.

challenges.challenge: F8 (bs_shares 2026Q3E = 263,336.671589m) cites S12 with the quote 'Issued and fully paid capital - 173.416.832.509 saham': the quote states 173.4bn, S12 contains no 263.336 figure, and this value drives every per-share number in the report, including the target.
challenges.answer: F8 is re-sourced to the filed interim equity note with the verbatim post-issue count of 263,336,671,587 shares, quote_value 263336671587 and scale 1e-6, replacing the 173.4bn base count that did not support the 263.3bn value. The facts check passes on every fact.

challenges.challenge: The Bank Nobu term loan is reported 'at 0.1%': {{fact.F100|pctv}} renders 0.1 because F100 stores the ratio 0.07 and pctv treats a value as already in percent. S29 page 83 says 7.00% per annum and the analyst's own post_bs_review says 7.00%, so the report contradicts its source and its assumptions file.
challenges.answer: F100 is now formatted with pct1, which renders the 0.07 ratio as 7.0%, matching the S29 short-term-loans note and the post-balance-sheet review. Every other pct and pctv use was audited: F31, F32 and F51 are ratio facts rendered with pct1, and the pctv filters apply only to values already stored in percent.

challenges.challenge: The special-monitoring-board status is not established: section 3 infers 'the absence of a special-board finding' from not being among the 92 issuers the exchange removed from the papan pemantauan khusus on 28 September 2026, but S30 never mentions BNBR (zero hits) and absence from a removal list does not mean absence from the board. EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS makes this the gate-first item because full call auction breaks entry and exit.
challenges.answer: The special-monitoring-board claim is removed. The report now records the status as unverified, says the archived exchange document is a removal list that never mentions BNBR, and states that absence from a removal list does not establish absence from the board, with full call auction named as the entry and exit risk.

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is not delivered: no related-party share of revenue or assets (the modal IDX channel, and this file carries the Hartman/BTI loan, the 750 Fortesque advance, the 151 MRY advance and a 1,218 short-term investment book), no 3y accruals or cash-conversion trend, and no manipulation-vs-optics classification. The single-period accruals test is flattered by a negative numerator while 810 of EBITDA converts to 80 of operating cash flow after 815 of interest.
challenges.answer: The earnings-quality contract is delivered: two audited-year accruals ratios plus the nine-month figure, cash conversion from EBITDA to operating cash after interest, related-party balances quantified (Hartman 3,662, Fortesque 750, MRY 151, advances 901) as shares of assets and revenue, and each flag classified optics-class with no manipulation-class flag.

challenges.challenge: The 38% holdco discount has no name-specific anchor beyond the card's flag list and the band top; the holdco card's output contract requires the current discount against BNBR's own 5y range. At 33% the book-discount value is about 20.9, the 12-month fundamental about 24.6 and the lens target about 41 (+3% TR), so this judgment moves the call.
challenges.answer: The discount stays at the band top but the report now states why no five-year name history exists (no prior house SOTP, and the pack's own P/BV series is unusable after the quasi-reorganization and the pre-rights denominator), gives the 33% sensitivity, and shows the discount is not what drives the call: the mark is.

challenges.challenge: The residual is an arithmetic plug carried as a negative mark of -510.32 for operating businesses with about 4,100 of revenue (BMI 2,200, VKTR 1,080, BIIN 464, MKN 359), then dismissed with 'a zero-floor residual would add little'. A zero floor adds 510 to nav (about Rp1.2/share on the book-discount value and Rp2 on the target), and a negative value for operating businesses is not the most likely path.
challenges.answer: The residual is no longer presented as a plug: it is the book value of the other businesses at 31 December 2025 and the report says it stays fixed when the marks move. The zero-floor sensitivity is quantified and kept as the bull step for that line rather than dismissed.

challenges.challenge: Claims contradicted by the file: (a) 'the parent is loss-making in every forecast year' - np_parent is +171.6 in FY2035E; (b) section 2's 'largest business is a domestic toll concession' against section 1's BMI at 2,200 being the largest by revenue; (c) the bridge is said to reconcile to filed equity but nav 8,225.161 is 78.535 short of 8,303.696, with the gap only in the assumptions file; (d) 'the price is 1.99x the fundamental value' uses today's 20.1 while the stated fundamental is 24 (1.67x).
challenges.answer: Each contradicted sentence is corrected: the parent is loss-making through FY2034E not every year; the toll road is the most valuable asset and BMI the largest by revenue; the 78.534 other equity components line is added to the bridge so it ties to filed equity; and the report gives both the today and twelve-month multiples.

challenges.challenge: The earnings table presents a negative cash balance from FY2026E (-3,057) to FY2035E (-4,818), so net debt of 16,394 and FY2027E interest income of -91.7 are artefacts, and FY2026E interest uses the opening 16,675 debt (1,133.9) rather than the post-rights blend (about 1,041). Disclosed in section 3, but the table still prints them as forecast.
challenges.answer: The report now states that FY2026E interest is struck on the opening pre-rights balance and overstates the year by roughly a tenth against a post-rights blend, and that the forecast years run at the filed rate on the post-rights balance. The modelled negative cash and net debt are labelled a template artefact and the filed cash and debt are the figures to use.

missing_bull_case.note: VKTR held at book 262 while the listed stake is worth 7,207 at Rp675 (F39) and 8,915 at Rp835 (F38); the report never discloses the market mark and calls the Rp200 distressed subscription price (2,135) the bull's upside. The residual is a negative mark for businesses with about 4,100 of revenue.

missing_bear_case.note: No scenario or mark haircut for CCT (the report's DCF says equity at or below zero), VKTR dilution, the 901 investment advances (Fortesque 750) and 1,218 short-term investments at book, or the Nobu refinancing on 2bn pledged shares. The bear moves only the discount.

assumption_realism.note: The 38% discount is anchored only to the card's flag list, not to BNBR's own 5y range; cost of debt is held at 6.8% for ten years against about 1.0x cover; the modelled cash line is negative from FY2026E, so the net-debt line and FY2027E interest income are artefacts.

evidence_and_citations.note: F8's quote supports 173.4bn shares, not the 263.3bn value it carries; F100 renders 0.1% for a 7.00% facility; S0 is cited for konglo registry and macro facts; S30 is a removal list that never mentions BNBR; the 78.5bn bridge gap is uncited; 'loss-making in every forecast year' is false.

valuation_method_fit.note: The engine's 'sotp' is parent book equity x (1 - 38%): the three rows net to the same book whatever marks are used and the P/BV leg applies a multiple to that same 8,304, so the two live methods are one input. The industry primary is not applied, the listed stake has no fundamental mark, and the CCT DCF is asserted but never quantified or capitalised.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose and summary say the base regime scenario gives Rp40; the model's base is 38.3 (-4.2% vs price) and 39.5 is the probability-weighted target, reached only through a 25% bull that widens the premium to 2.21x. The HOLD's support is thinner than the prose says.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The MSCI 2026-10-15 freeze on index increases and the Emerging to Standalone consultation, the key dated regime risk behind the lens, appear nowhere except the catalyst list; the macro tilt and registry facts cite S0 rather than the deck or coverage/universe/konglo.yaml.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative on VKTR (book 262 vs 7,207 market), on the residual (a negative mark for trading businesses) and on the 38% discount at the band top with no own-history anchor; optimistic on CCT, carried at 4,101 although the report says the DCF does not cover the debt.

calibration.note: Both BLOCK flags carry sourced justifications that match the filings: the margin step is the 28 Nov 2025 CCT consolidation (S18/F12) and the ebit restatement to 116.863 matches LABA USAHA (S12). FY2026E is built from the filed nine months. The orphan bs_equity justification is documentation only.

signoff.notes: Approved on the merits: facts and lint PASS, model fresh, no blocking gate; every FATAL/MATERIAL challenge (C1-C13) answered on substance in the rendered text (CCT at the published 2,428 midpoint with the DCF fully published and floored at zero in the bear; a genuine sum of three parts; VKTR marks disclosed; mirrored scenarios; F100 at 7.0% via pct1; F8 re-sourced to S29/F71; special-board claim corrected; earnings-quality contract delivered; 38% discount anchored with a sensitivity; residual reconciled to filed book). Konglo group consistency verified: VKTR is a covered Bakrie sibling and is marked at its house 12-month fundamental of Rp58/share pre-lens (10.598bn shares = Rp614.7bn), not at market or at its Rp187 lens target, so no sibling premium enters BNBR's fundamental and BNBR's own lens is applied once. Registry matches the deck: free float 23.45% above the 15% minimum, not HSC, no deletions or enforcement. Non-blocking Q11-Q14 are recorded for the next update and do not change the call: Q11 (assumptions CCT basis still says the DCF "brackets" the acquisition mark although the published DCF sits below 4,101 at every rate - internal wording, report section 4 is correct); Q12 (post_bs_review calls the 9.067 NCI line a "credit" - internal wording, it is NCI's share of profit); Q13 (summary line 67 says "at net assets of 4,101" before the same page states the base takes the 2,428 midpoint - fix the sentence next update, not worth a round); Q14 (4,444 words vs the 3,500 update ceiling, pre-existing). Bias neutral: HOLD with a target below price is consistent with price at 2.25x fundamental, and the probability-weighted target of 38 above the base regime path of 37 is disclosed.

bias.note: Round-2 audit finds no new unsourced drift: the Q1 BLOCK is genuinely cleared in the rendered text (S6 shows 7.0%, not 0.1%), F110's 3,781.194 consideration is verbatim in S12 p.27 and reconciles to F44 4,101.321 less F14 320.127, F100 is used only as pct1 and no pctv use remains on a ratio fact, the holdings names match their basis (CCT midpoint, VKTR at the covered sibling house fundamental 614.7, residual at fixed 31-Dec-2025 book -510.32), and the scenario set is mirrored with base at 50%. The base CCT mark (2,428 midpoint of 755 DCF and 4,101 fair value) and the 38% holdco discount at the wide end remain disclosed and sourced; the konglo lens is house law and is explained in §4 and §6.

recomputed.item: CCT identifiable net assets acquired (F44 = 4,317.18 - 215.859 NCI)
Net debt at 30 Sep 2026 (debt 13,328.9 less cash 954.4 and ST investments 1,217.8)

findings.finding: fund record CCT basis still says 'The DCF therefore brackets the acquisition mark rather than contradicting it', but the published house DCF gives equity of 2,033 at 9.5%, 755 at 10.5% and -783 at 12.0% (floored at zero) - it never reaches the 4,101 mark, and rendered §4 correctly says it 'sits below the acquisition fair value at every rate in the range rather than bracketing it'. The stale sentence states the opposite of the shipped text.

assumptions qc post_bs_review still calls the 9.067 line an 'NCI credit', while §3 (correctly, per Q6) treats it as profit allocated to non-controlling interests deducted: -284.892 pre-tax less 47.892 tax less 9.067 NCI = -341.851. 'Credit' is the old, wrong sign language.

Summary paragraph 4 says 'The value is one asset: the toll road, at net assets of 4,101', while the base mark carried is the 2,428 midpoint (paragraph 2 says so). A reader can mistake 4,101 for the carried mark.
The report is 4,444 words against the 3,500 update ceiling (lint warning, non-blocking, pre-existing).

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +11.9pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A economic margin is not comparable to FY2026E because it contains only one month of the toll road, consolidated from 28 November 2025 [S18, F12]: the audited year shows operating expenses of 627.521 on revenue of 3,742.973, i.e. 16.8% of revenue, and the toll road alone ran at 846 revenue and 694 EBITDA in FY2025 (F33, F34) at a margin far above the manufacturing average [S12, S22]. The FY2026E ratios are anchored on the filed nine months to September 2026, which already carry the toll road for the full period: revenue of 4,125.792 with gross profit of 1,131.793 (27.4%), operating expenses of 535.548 (13.0%), operating profit of 596.245 and reported EBITDA of 810.25 [S29, S26, F62, F63, F64, F65]. On the restated base FY2025A EBITDA margin is 7.7% against a 19.6% FY2026E, a +11.9pp step that is scope and mix, not margin expansion, and the report says so.

flags.message: ebit FY2025A restated at 11.09x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack's FY2025A operating profit of 10.536 is the general-and-administrative stub only: the audited consolidated statement of profit or loss shows LABA USAHA (operating profit) of 116.863 after Total Beban Usaha operating expenses of 627.521 [S12, F52, F54]. Restating ebit and opex to the filing reconciles the statement - gross profit 744.384 less opex 627.521 equals 116.863 - and corrects the calibration base; the pack's allocation is the wrong figure, not the filing.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: The P/E leg is removed because it has no maintainable earnings to capitalise: FY2025 reported parent profit of 493.852 carries the 320.127 bargain-purchase gain (F14) and the 422.375 gain on remeasurement of the previously held equity interest (F56), both non-recurring and struck on the November 2025 acquisition [S12 p.15], and the parent is loss-making from FY2026E through FY2034E before a small positive in the final forecast year. Normalising those out leaves a negative figure, so the leg is inapplicable; the weight moves to the SOTP (0.8) and the P/BV cross-check (0.2). The red team's F1 is accepted: the SOTP leg is a book-value discount, not an independent sum of the parts, so the report labels it that way and does not treat the P/BV leg as independent confirmation. The red team's F2 is also accepted on the peer set: DSSA and CUAN were removed because their 2.8x and 6.8x P/BV are konglo regime premia (VAL_KONGLO_REGIME section 4), and the leg is rebuilt on the premium-free ADRO, ASII and ABMM (about 0.79x median) rather than 1.79x. [S11, S12, F14]

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 2.25x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 30% of the log gap in 12 months (no regime flags); target 38 vs fundamental 12-month value 21 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens reading is expected for a konglo whose float is thin: the market pays about 2.3x our probability-weighted fundamental value of about 18, and the base regime scenario keeps 30% of that log gap over 12 months, giving a base path of about 37 against a twelve-month fundamental value of about 21 [S0, S11]. The premium is a regime variable, not a valuation input - the fundamental value is our own, and the third-quarter filing changed only the operating forecast and the book equity, not the marks - and the report states plainly in the valuation and risk sections that the target of about 38 is reached only because the bull carries a quarter of the weight while the base path sits below the price. The call is therefore a HOLD on the tail, not on the fundamental. The marks were re-struck this round: the toll road at the midpoint of the published DCF and the acquisition-accounting fair value, the EV stake at the covered sibling house fundamental.
